mainRepository.heading: GitHub connection and main repository
mainRepository.about: The main repository is where this workspace keeps .oxagen/: its published steering records, the promotion ledger, and every agent definition. A workspace has one. Until it is bound the workspace is provisional: runs are still recorded and spend still counts, but steering and agent definitions stay off.
mainRepository.connected: Returned from GitHub. The installation is attached to this workspace.
mainRepository.installRefused: Returned from GitHub, but that installation could not be verified, so nothing was attached. Install the App again from this workspace and approve it on the account that owns the repository.
mainRepository.installUnverified: Returned from GitHub with the App installed, but GitHub sent no authorization to check the installation against, so nothing has been attached yet. Use “Connect an existing installation” below to finish. The App is already installed, so it takes one click and no further approval.

install.heading: Oxagen reaches a repository through its GitHub App
install.body: No installation is attached to this workspace yet, so there is nothing to pick from. Install the App on the account that owns the repository, or connect an installation that account already has; GitHub sends you back here either way.
install.unreachable: An installation is attached to this workspace, but GitHub would not let Oxagen use it. That is what an uninstalled, suspended, or withdrawn installation looks like from here. Install the App again, or attach an installation this account still reaches. Either one replaces the installation on file.

mainRepository.unconfigured: This deployment has no GitHub App configured, so the App cannot be installed from here. An operator sets the App up before a repository can be bound.

picker.heading: Pick this workspace's main repository
picker.loading: Listing the repositories the installation reaches…
picker.empty: The installation reaches no repositories. Grant it access to one on GitHub, then reload this page.
picker.truncated: The installation reaches more repositories than this list holds, so the one you want may not be here. Narrow the App's repository access on GitHub and reload this page.

bound.heading: Bound
bound.retired: The GitHub connection this repository was bound through has been removed, so Oxagen can no longer read .oxagen/ from it. Steering and Context PRs are off until it is bound again. The repository itself has not changed, and neither has anything else about this workspace. Bind it again through a live GitHub connection.
bound.fixed: Which repository is main cannot be changed here. Moving a workspace to another repository is an organization owner's decision, needs approval, and is recorded as a security event.
bound.refDrift: Context PRs are opened against, checked against, and merged into the branch approved here, never whatever GitHub currently calls the default. If this repository's default branch was renamed, they are refused until the new branch is approved.

mainRepository.manage: Change which repositories the App reaches
mainRepository.installChoose: Returned from GitHub. This account reaches more than one installation of the Oxagen App, so pick the one this workspace should act through.
mainRepository.installNone: Returned from GitHub. The Oxagen App is not installed on any account you administer, so there is nothing to attach yet. Install it on the account that owns the repository.

installations.heading: Installations this account reaches
installations.about: The App is already installed on these accounts. Pick the one this workspace should reach repositories through.
installations.loading: Listing the installations this account reaches…
installations.listLabel: GitHub accounts the App is installed on

failure.denied: Only an organization Owner or Admin, or this workspace’s Owner, can read or change this workspace’s repositories.
failure.githubNotConnected: No GitHub App installation is attached to this workspace, so there is nothing to bind. Install the App first.
failure.repositoryNotInstalled: The installation cannot read that repository. Grant it access on GitHub, then try again.
failure.mainRepoBound: This workspace already binds a different main repository. Changing it is an org owner's decision, recorded as a security event.
failure.invalid: That repository name is not one GitHub accepts.
failure.pendingApproval: This needs a person to approve it. Request {accessRequestId} is waiting.
failure.unavailable: This could not be read from GitHub ({code}). Try again in a moment.
failure.githubNotAuthorized: GitHub is not authorized for this organization yet, so there is nothing to list. Connect GitHub first.
failure.installationUnreachable: The connected GitHub account cannot reach that installation. Pick one it can, or install the App on that account.
failure.mainRepo: That is this workspace’s main repository. It is bound above, and a main repository is never also linked.
failure.repositoryAlreadyLinked: That repository is already linked to this workspace.
failure.mainRepoClaimed: Another workspace steers by that repository. A workspace’s main repository cannot be linked by another workspace, because Context PRs would open on its .oxagen/ tree.
failure.mainRepoUnbound: Bind this workspace’s main repository first. A linked repository is its second.
failure.repositoryLinkedElsewhere: Another workspace has linked that repository, so it cannot be this workspace’s main. A main repository holds the .oxagen/ tree, and a linked one receives another workspace’s Context PRs.
failure.mainRepoUnlinkRefused: The main repository cannot be unlinked. A workspace without one cannot exist.
failure.repositoryNotLinked: That repository is no longer linked to this workspace. Reload the page to read the current list.
failure.branchNotFound: GitHub has no branch by that name in this repository. Check the spelling, or push the branch first.
failure.productionBranchMissing: The production branch this repository records no longer exists on GitHub. Set the production branch first.
failure.productionBranchIsInitBranch: This repository records oxagen/init as its production branch, which is where the init pull request is pushed. Set another production branch first.
failure.oxagenTreeExists: This repository already has .oxagen/ on its production branch. Change it with an ordinary pull request.
failure.governanceTomlInvalid: governance.toml does not declare the mode you chose. Fix the file or pick the mode it names.
failure.workspaceTomlInvalid: workspace.toml is not valid TOML. Fix the file and open the pull request again.
failure.secretFound: A file carries a credential or personal data. Nothing was pushed. Take it out and open the pull request again.
failure.authorityDeclared: A file declares a grant of authority, which the init tree never carries. Nothing was pushed. Take it out and open the pull request again.
failure.githubRefused: GitHub refused the write. Nothing reached the production branch. Check that the App can write to this repository, then try again.

page.title: Repositories
page.subtitle: Where this workspace’s files live and every change Oxagen has proposed to them.

error.title: Repositories could not be loaded
error.body: The control plane answered {answer}. Nothing was changed. Runs kept recording while this page was down. Frames are written by the collector on each host, not by Oxagen.
error.incidentNotRecorded: Opening an incident from this page is not recorded yet. Report the code and the time below.

denied.title: You cannot see this workspace’s repositories
denied.body: Your roles on {org} do not include {needed}. An organization owner can grant it; the grant is a governed action and lands in the audit record with your name on it.
denied.requestNotRecorded: Requesting access from this page is not recorded yet. Ask an organization owner for {needed}.
denied.decidedBy: the organization's policy · deny wins over every allow

empty.title: This workspace has no repository yet
empty.body: A workspace without a main repo cannot exist, so this state is the moment between creating one and binding it. The main repo is where steering and configuration are managed in source control. Until it is bound, there is nowhere for a record to be published to.

repos.bannerBadge: {count, plural, one {# linked repository carries} other {# linked repositories carry}} no .oxagen/
repos.bannerLead: A run on {repositories} is steered by the main repo and by nothing of its own.
repos.bannerBody: Repository-scoped records live in that repository, so until it has a .oxagen/ tree there is nowhere to put one, and a record that tried would have to claim workspace scope, which the checks refuse.
repos.title: Repositories
repos.subtitle: One main repo, any number of linked. The main repo holds the workspace’s steering and configuration; a linked repo may hold records that steer only runs on it.
repos.label: Repositories this workspace can see
repos.retired: Connection retired. Open the repository to bind it again through a live connection.
repos.reachableUnread: The repositories this installation reaches could not be listed, so only bound ones are shown.
repos.truncated: The installation reaches more repositories than this list holds. Narrow the App's repository access on GitHub to see the rest.
repos.note: Changing which repository is main is an organization-owner action with approval, and it lands in the audit record as a security event. The production branch never moves on its own: when GitHub’s default branch changes, the App records it and prompts, and the binding stays where it is until somebody confirms.

facts.filesAt: · {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} at {sha}

dialog.recordsMain: Scope is workspace. These steer every run in {workspace}.
dialog.recordsLinked: Scope is repository. These steer only runs whose repository binding is this one. A record here may narrow what a workspace record allows; it may never widen it, and one that claimed workspace scope would fail the checks.
dialog.noTreeAvailable: This repository is not linked to {workspace} either. Adding Oxagen to it is what links it.
dialog.noTreeLinked: Runs on this repository are steered by {main} and by nothing of its own. There is nowhere to publish a repository-scoped record until the tree exists.
dialog.initOpen: Pull request #{number} adds .oxagen/ and is waiting for a person to merge it.
dialog.linked: {repository} linked to {workspace}. Its issues and events reach this workspace, and a run may bind to it.

branch.heading: Production branch
branch.about: The only branch whose commits update the code graph, the only one .oxagen/ is read from, and the only one a pull request from Oxagen merges into. It never moves on its own.
branch.moved: GitHub’s default branch is {github}. The production branch is still {current}.
branch.label: Another branch
branch.changed: The production branch moved from {from} to {to}. Runs admitted before the change keep citing {from}.
branch.unchanged: {branch} is already the production branch. Nothing was written.

unlink.title: Unlink {repository} from {workspace}?
unlink.body: Its issues and events stop reaching this workspace, and a run can no longer bind to it here. The repository is untouched: nothing is deleted, no branch moves, and .oxagen/ stays where it is.
unlink.governed: Records published in this repository stop steering runs in {workspace} the moment this is written. Runs already recorded keep naming the hashes they carried.
unlink.copies: Working copies linked through it are not recorded yet, so this cannot say how many stop appearing on the Working copies tab.
unlink.done: {repository} unlinked from {workspace}. Runs already recorded keep naming it; nothing new binds to it here.

copies.title: Working copies
copies.subtitle: The same .oxagen/ tree on a machine. Each is a directory somebody ran oxagen init in; the enrollment is the machine’s, and the link is one gitignored file.
copies.notRecorded: No working copy is recorded yet. oxagen init links a directory on a machine and reports nothing back to Oxagen, so this table stays empty until it does.
copies.filesToml: # committed. reviewed. the source of truth.
copies.filesNote: The committed file says what the workspace is. The gitignored one says which workspace this checkout is talking to, which is a fact about a laptop and not about the product, so it is never reviewed, never merged, and never the same file in two places.

sync.init: Links this directory. Reads the git remote and writes .oxagen/workspace.json. Idempotent.
sync.pull: Not in the CLI yet. git pull on the production branch updates .oxagen/ today.
sync.status: What this copy has against what is published: the files under .oxagen/ that are behind or changed here.
sync.propose: Turns a local edit under .oxagen/ into a proposal. Opening and merging its pull request happen here, because both gate on a role only a signed-in person holds.

copies.syncNote: Stella symlinks into this directory rather than copying it, so there is no second copy that could drift. A copy whose symlinks read missing is one where Stella will load nothing.
copies.stale: A copy that is behind is not a run that is behind. Steering reaches a run from the merged commit, whatever a directory on a laptop holds.
copies.label: Working copies of this workspace

linkdir.title: Connect a directory
linkdir.subtitle: one command, run in the directory
linkdir.lead: Run this in the directory you want linked. It reads the git remote, matches it against the repositories this installation can reach, and writes the one gitignored file that says which workspace this checkout talks to.
linkdir.pairingHint: Oxagen does not issue pairing codes yet, so the directory is linked on the machine only and does not appear on the Working copies tab.
linkdir.whatLabel: What it writes, and what it does not

writes.name: writes
writes.what: .oxagen/workspace.json: org, workspace, path, machine. Gitignored, never reviewed, never merged.

links.name: links
links.what: .stella/rules, .stella/proposals and .stella/agents as symlinks into .oxagen/, so there is no second copy that could drift.

noWrite.name: does not write
noWrite.what: anything under .oxagen/ that is committed. If the repository has no .oxagen/ tree at all, it says so and offers the pull request that adds one.

noRead.name: does not read
noRead.what: your working tree. Oxagen reads .oxagen/ and nothing else; what a run needs from the rest of the repository reaches it as frames, at the hooks.

linkdir.grants: Linking a directory grants nothing. A person’s roles decide what they may do here, and an agent’s mandate decides what it may do there; a laptop is not a principal.
linkdir.copyFailed: Copying did not work. Select the command and copy it.

changes.title: Open Context PRs
changes.subtitle: Four kinds of file and one lifecycle. Whoever opened it (a person, the promoter, or the reconciler), the checks, the merge and the publication are the same.
changes.label: Pull requests Oxagen opened
changes.loading: Reading the pull requests Oxagen has open
changes.empty: Oxagen has no pull request open or merged on this workspace’s repositories.
changes.otherKinds: Context records are the only kind listed here today. Init, skill, agent, tool and configuration pull requests have no list yet.
changes.note: A change is in force from the merge commit, not from when it was written. While a pull request is open the thing it carries steers nothing: it is not in the compiled bundle, not in the record index, and the bundle version has not moved.

promoter.name: the promoter
promoter.what: Aggregates records across runs by lineage and opens a proposal with the runs it cites. There is no threshold; a person reads the support and decides.

reconciler.name: the reconciler
reconciler.what: Reads .oxagen/workspace.toml against what the control plane has, and opens one pull request per real difference. It never edits live state to match the file. It is not built yet.

person.name: a person
person.what: Every creation wizard (agent, tool, skill, record) ends here. None of them has a Save button that ends in a database.

changes.drift: Drift is reported, never repaired in place. A reconciler that silently edited either side would make the file a description of the past and the product unreviewable, and the pull request is the only place a person can say which of the two was right.

change.stopped: {check} stopped the run. {summary} The checks behind it stayed queued, merge is disabled, and nothing was published.

merge.squash: Squash the branch onto {base}, pinned to the commit the checks ran on.
merge.reindex: Re-index from the merged commit and bump the workspace bundle version from v{current} to v{after}.
merge.ledger: Append the promotion event to the ledger, with the approver and the commit sha.
merge.audit: Write one audit event. The change is in force from that commit, not from now.

change.waiting: Merge stays disabled until every check reports.
change.merged: Merged. The file is on {base}, the promotion event is on the ledger, and the workspace’s steering version is the ledger’s length.
change.mergedDone: Merged at {commit}. The change is in force from that commit.
change.didNotRun: Did not run: {check} stopped the run.

closepr.title: Close {pr}
closepr.subtitle: without merging
closepr.lead: The pull request closes on GitHub and nothing is published. Oxagen posts this comment on it:
closepr.notPosted: Posting this comment is not recorded yet: Oxagen closes the pull request and records the comment as the reason, and GitHub shows no comment.
closepr.note: Closing is a governed action: it is recorded in Audit with your name, and the branch is deleted with it.

config.noMain: This workspace binds no main repository, so there is no .oxagen/ to show.
config.workspaceMissing: Not on the production branch yet. Add Oxagen to this repository to put it there.
config.driftSubtitle: The file against what the control plane has. Reported, never repaired in place.
config.driftNotRecorded: Not recorded yet. Drift is the reconciler’s record of the file against what the control plane holds, and the reconciler is not built. When it is, drift arrives as a pull request, never as an edit in place.
config.governanceMissing: No governance.toml on the production branch. Pull requests are reviewed as team.

modes.solo: The author may merge their own.
modes.team: A reviewer other than the author merges: an org Owner or Admin, or a workspace Owner. This is what a missing file means.
modes.regulated: An org Owner or Admin other than the author merges, recorded as the accountable approver.

mode.invalid: no mode Oxagen knows: opening and merging are refused

config.modeNote: The mode is read on the production branch when a pull request is opened and again when it is merged, so raising it takes effect on everything still open, and it is changed by a pull request like everything else, never by a settings screen. A file that exists but names no mode refuses both, rather than quietly falling back to team.
config.treeJson: workspace.json is gitignored and never on the production branch.
config.treeNote: Oxagen reads .oxagen/ and nothing else. Whatever sits under .stella/ is invisible to it, and it never looks.

wizard.title: Add Oxagen to a repository
wizard.subtitle: the directory every other file needs

repository.lead: Oxagen governs the files in a repository; it does not keep a copy of them. So the first thing it does in a repository is put the directory there: on a branch, in a pull request, which somebody reads.
repository.label: Repository
repository.hint: Only repositories the installation can already reach, and only the ones with no .oxagen/ yet. A repository that has one is already governed; changing it is an ordinary pull request from the page it belongs to.
repository.empty: No repository the installation reaches is without .oxagen/. Every one is governed already, or the installation reaches nothing yet.
repository.noMain: This workspace binds no main repo yet. Connect GitHub and bind the main repo first; the wizard continues from there.

main.title: Make it the main repo
main.about: The workspace’s steering and configuration live here. Exactly one per workspace, and moving it is an owner action with approval.

linked.title: Link it
linked.about: Its agents work on it. It may carry records that steer only runs on this repository, and never records that claim the workspace.

repository.noteLinked: {main} is already this workspace’s main repo, so this one is linked.
repository.moveMain: Moving the main repo to another repository is an organization-owner action with approval, and no capability performs it yet.

branch.lead: Two things are decided once here, and both are then changed the way everything else is: by a pull request against this repository.
branch.label: Production branch
branch.hint: GitHub’s default branch is {branch}, which is the suggestion and not the decision. This is the only branch whose commits update the code graph, and the only one a record is published to. If GitHub’s default changes later, Oxagen records it and prompts; the binding never moves on its own.
branch.modeHint: This is read off .oxagen/rules/governance.toml when a pull request is opened and again when it is merged, so raising it takes effect on everything already in flight. Nothing else in Oxagen writes that file.

modes.solo: The author may merge their own. One person, or a repository nobody else reviews.
modes.team: A reviewer other than the author merges. What a missing governance.toml means, and what most repositories want.
modes.regulated: An org Owner or Admin other than the author merges, recorded as the accountable approver. The author of a record may never be its approver.

permissions.lead: What Oxagen will be able to do in {repository}
permissions.label: GitHub App permissions

contents.name: Contents
contents.for: the branch and the file every pull request carries

pullRequests.name: Pull requests
pullRequests.for: opening one, and re-reading its head before a merge

checks.name: Checks
checks.for: the check runs on the head commit

issues.name: Issues
issues.for: task references, so spend rolls up to an issue

permissions.cannotLabel: And what it still cannot do

push.name: push to {branch}
push.what: Every write is to a branch. The production branch changes only by a merge somebody performed.

merge.name: merge on its own
merge.what: Merging gates on a role only a signed-in person holds, under the mode this repository declares.

secret.name: read a secret
secret.what: The scan refuses a pull request that carries one. Nothing in .oxagen/ holds a credential; a server is named there and its credential lives in the vault.

authority.name: grant authority
authority.what: Nothing in this tree can grant a tool, raise a tier or lift a budget. A record steers; a belt grants.

review.note: Every line is yours to change before anybody reviews it. What lands is what the pull request carries, not what this screen drafted.

pullRequest.lead: The pull request puts the directory in {repository}. Until somebody merges it, this repository is ungoverned and nothing here is in force, which is also the only place a reviewer can stop it.

workspaceToml.main: the workspace, its repos, servers and budgets

checks.schema: workspace.toml parses, and every repository it declares resolves through this installation.
checks.layout: No .oxagen/ exists on {branch}. Nothing is overwritten, and a repository that already has one is refused rather than merged into.
checks.governance: mode = {mode} is one of the three. A file that parses but names no mode would refuse every later pull request, so it is refused now.
checks.secret_pii_scan: No credential, key, email or personal datum in any added file.
checks.no_authority: Nothing added grants a tool, raises a tier or lifts a budget.

opened.reused: {repository}#{number} already adds .oxagen/. Nothing new was pushed.
opened.merge: Merging it is yours. Once it merges, this repository reads as governed here.
